cards.front: sound
cards.back: Something you hear with your ears.
cards.say: sound. Something you hear with your ears.

cards.front: loud
cards.back: A loud sound is easy to hear. Thunder is loud.
cards.say: loud. A loud sound is easy to hear. Thunder is loud.

cards.front: quiet
cards.back: A quiet sound is soft and hard to hear. A whisper is quiet.
cards.say: quiet. A quiet sound is soft and hard to hear. A whisper is quiet.

cards.front: vibrate
cards.back: To shake very fast. Things that make sounds vibrate.
cards.say: vibrate. To shake very fast. Things that make sounds vibrate.

cards.front: drum
cards.back: You hit it to make a sound.
cards.say: drum. You hit it to make a sound.

cards.front: bell
cards.back: It rings when you shake it or hit it.
cards.say: bell. It rings when you shake it or hit it.

cards.front: guitar
cards.back: You pluck its strings to make a sound.
cards.say: guitar. You pluck its strings to make a sound.

cards.front: voice
cards.back: The sound you make with your mouth when you talk or sing.
cards.say: voice. The sound you make with your mouth when you talk or sing.

cards.front: Which one is loud: a whisper or a siren?
cards.back: A siren.
cards.say: Which one is loud: a whisper or a siren? A siren.

cards.front: Which one is quiet: a mouse or a thunderstorm?
cards.back: A mouse.
cards.say: Which one is quiet: a mouse or a thunderstorm? A mouse.

cards.front: What makes the sound of a drum?
cards.back: Hitting the drum makes it shake and make a sound.
cards.say: What makes the sound of a drum? Hitting the drum makes it shake and make a sound.

cards.front: What do we use to hear sounds?
cards.back: Our ears.
cards.say: What do we use to hear sounds? Our ears.

cards.front: What happens to a sound when you walk away?
cards.back: It gets quieter.
cards.say: What happens to a sound when you walk away? It gets quieter.

cards.front: What happens to a sound when you come closer?
cards.back: It gets louder.
cards.say: What happens to a sound when you come closer? It gets louder.

cards.front: Which animal makes a sound that goes meow?
cards.back: A cat.
cards.say: Which animal makes a sound that goes meow? A cat.

cards.front: Which animal makes a sound that goes moo?
cards.back: A cow.
cards.say: Which animal makes a sound that goes moo? A cow.

cards.front: Which animal makes a sound that goes quack?
cards.back: A duck.
cards.say: Which animal makes a sound that goes quack? A duck.

cards.front: Which sound source is a living thing: a bird or a bell?
cards.back: A bird. A bell is not alive.
cards.say: Which sound source is a living thing: a bird or a bell? A bird. A bell is not alive.

cards.front: Which sound source is non-living: a radio or a dog?
cards.back: A radio.
cards.say: Which sound source is non-living: a radio or a dog? A radio.

cards.front: What sound does a clap make?
cards.back: A clap makes a loud, sharp sound.
cards.say: What sound does a clap make? A clap makes a loud, sharp sound.

cards.front: How can you make a drum sound quieter?
cards.back: Tap it softly.
cards.say: How can you make a drum sound quieter? Tap it softly.

cards.front: Why should we not listen to very loud sounds?
cards.back: Very loud sounds can hurt our ears.
cards.say: Why should we not listen to very loud sounds? Very loud sounds can hurt our ears.
